claim: *Engineer–agent interaction through Modeling and Alignment.* Engineers communicate intent and knowledge through natural language, specifications, and models; delegated realization returns evidence through review, testing, and analysis. The channels are complementary rather than sequential. Modeling makes selected engineering knowledge available to guide realization; Alignment evaluates the resulting work against engineering obligations and governs which actions or results may proceed.
topology: Two parallel channel fans joined by a single implementation hinge; intent descends and evidence returns.
required_terms: what do I know, intend, and need to make explicit?
what does the evidence justify believing or doing?
bw_encoding: White nodes and panels; bare bold mode headings and italic question annotations; no heading boxes.
redesign: Author-requested side clearance: widen the outer frames and shift each unchanged channel group outward by 0.2 cm. Native side clearance increases from approximately 0.6 pt to 9.2 pt, comparable to the existing top/bottom margins. Preserve all labels, fonts, inner box dimensions, arrow directions, vertical geometry, and shared implementation hinge. Apply equivalent 20 px side margins in the web SVG.
alt:
Two panels over one shared implementation node. Left panel, Modeling / Communicating:
    the engineer fans out through three parallel channels — natural language, specification, and models —
    which converge on the agent; the agent produces the implementation. Right panel, Alignment /
    Evaluating: the implementation yields a result, which fans out through three parallel channels —
    review, testing, and analysis — that converge back on the engineer. The same engineer appears at both
    upper ends; the single implementation node at the bottom is the hinge between communicating intent
    and evaluating evidence.
